observation.visible_scene: A low-angle sunset view over a calm body of water. A transparent crystal lens-ball rests motionless on a bed of wet, dark pebbles in the left foreground, refracting an upside-down image of the horizon and a bright sliver of the sun. The sun sits just above a distant flat shoreline, throwing a vertical golden glitter-path across the water; the sky is warm orange-pink with thin clouds. The framing of the ball, the horizon line, and the sun stays fixed from the first to the last sampled frame.
visible_changes: The sun's glitter-path on the water continuously shimmers and breaks apart as small ripples move across the surface, so its shape and brightness fluctuate frame to frame while its position stays the same.

Reflections and sheen on the wet pebbles in the foreground shift subtly, and a thin film of water appears to creep/retreat over the pebbles to the right of the ball, changing how glossy that area looks over the excerpt.
The crystal ball itself does not roll, translate, or rotate; its internal refracted sun-spot and the dark reflection on its upper surface remain in the same place throughout.
The camera is essentially static: the ball-to-sun horizontal spacing and the horizon's vertical position do not change, so observed motion is in the water, not the viewpoint.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the ball was placed or moved before this segment, and whether any wave later reaches or displaces it.
The longer-term progression of the sunset (sun continuing to lower) beyond these ~2.7 seconds.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent advance/recede of the thin water film on the foreground pebbles is a real small wash or merely a change in specular shimmer from ripples.
Any sub-pixel camera drift is too small to confirm from the background evidence.
